title: Chameleons change colour by retuning tiny crystals in their skin

cover.alt: A green male panther chameleon with dark bands and a pale blue stripe grips a twig against a black background.
cover.credit: Teyssier J, Saenko S, van der Marel D, Milinkovitch M · CC BY 4.0

body: Besides yellow pigment, a male panther chameleon's skin holds cells packed with a lattice of **guanine nanocrystals**. The gaps between the crystals decide which colour the lattice reflects: packed closely, it reflects short, blue wavelengths, and the skin looks green. When the lizard gets excited, for example at the sight of a rival male, the crystals move apart and reflect longer wavelengths, turning the skin yellow and orange within a couple of minutes. When it calms down, the change reverses.

slides.alt: A green, banded panther chameleon on a twig turns yellow with deep red bands, while a small inset in the corner shows it as it looked at the start.
slides.caption: A male panther chameleon turns from green to yellow and red after another male was put in its sight. The researchers sped the film up 8×; the inset shows how it looked at the start.
slides.credit: Teyssier J, Saenko S, van der Marel D, Milinkovitch M · CC BY 4.0 · excerpt, sped up 8× by the authors

steps.label: With the yellow pigment, skin looks green

slides.label: smaller gaps between the crystals at rest than when excited
slides.text: The crystals themselves stay the same size, about 127 nanometres across. Only the spacing between them changes.

left.label: Pigment
left.text: Chameleons of both sexes and all ages can get lighter or darker by spreading out or gathering the pigment in their skin cells.

right.label: Crystals
right.text: The fast switch of hue, from green to yellow or orange, comes from changing the spacing of the crystal lattice.

slides.question: Which panther chameleons can make the fast green-to-orange switch?
slides.explanation: The crystal layer that does it is fully developed only in the skin of adult males. Females and young can still change brightness using pigment.
